title: A 1913 Rope-Pulling Study Explains Why Big Groups Coast
alt_title_1: The Ringelmann Effect: How 8-Person Teams Lose Half Their Power
alt_title_2: Why Tiny Single-Owner Teams Outship Bloated Committees
description_hook: In 1913, French engineer Maximilien Ringelmann measured how hard men pulled a rope alone versus in groups. By the time group size hit 8, per-person effort fell to 49%. Here is why lean teams and solo operators win on speed.

affiliate_cta.pinned_comment: Have you ever accomplished more alone in 90 minutes than an 8-person committee did in 3 weeks? Grab our Lean Operating System guide here: https://kenvh0010-lang.github.io/admin/bio/

scenes.headline: 8 People Pulling Half as Hard as 1
scenes.stat_label: INDIVIDUAL OUTPUT DROP FROM SOLO TO 8-PERSON GROUP
bullets: 8 pullers together average under half per person
scenes.narration: Put one person on a rope and they pull at full strength. Put eight people on that rope and half vanishes.
scenes.source: Maximilien Ringelmann, Annales de l'Institut National Agronomique (1913)

scenes.headline: Maximilien Ringelmann's 1913 Dynamometer Data
bullets: Pairs held 93% efficiency; trios slipped to 85%
Coordination friction + diffused blame halved effort at 8
scenes.narration: French agricultural engineer Maximilien Ringelmann published the exact numbers in 1913: solo pullers delivered one hundred percent of their capacity, pairs dropped to ninety-three percent, and groups of eight averaged forty-nine percent.
scenes.source: Ringelmann, 'Recherches sur les moteurs animes', Annales INA (1913)

scenes.headline: Committees Recreate Ringelmann's Rope Daily
scenes.left_body: Blurred blame + endless sync calls -> 49% effort per seat
scenes.right_body: 1 builder + automated software -> 100% clarity & fast shipping
scenes.narration: Modern offices recreate Ringelmann's rope every morning: eight-person status calls blur individual ownership, multiply coordination friction, and make coasting invisible inside the crowd.

scenes.headline: Assign One Clear Owner Per Deliverable
scenes.stat_label: TINY AUTONOMOUS UNITS COMPOUND SHIPPING VELOCITY
scenes.stat_subtext: 1-2 human owners + code automation -> zero coordination drag
scenes.narration: Protect single-threaded ownership: assign one clear builder per deliverable, keep working units to one or two people, and automate routine handoffs with software.

scenes.headline: Shrink the Rope to Multiply Output
bullets: Never invite 8 people to solve a 2-person task
Measure shipped artifacts, not meeting attendance
scenes.narration: Shrink the rope until every name owns a measurable outcome, and tiny teams outship bloated departments.
scenes.source: Mind & Margin operating rule based on Ringelmann (1913)
